title: Silent message loss — local send to a `Present` receiver drops on `HeapFull` instead of collecting, and the `Executing` ETF path drops captured-variable closures
purpose:
SILENT MESSAGE LOSS IS THE WORST WRONG-QUIETLY CLASS IN THIS VM. A crash is loud, an exception is catchable, a wrong answer is at least a wrong answer you can see. A dropped message is none of those: the receiver waits forever in `receive`, the supervisor sees a healthy process, the gen_server call times out somewhere else entirely, and nothing in the tree — no log line, no exit reason, no test — connects the timeout to the drop. In a VM whose entire correctness model rests on `!` being reliable, a reachable silent drop is a foundational break, and BEAM's guarantee is exactly the one being broken: `!` does not fail, and it does not lose the message either. beamr currently keeps the first half of that promise by abandoning the second.

Ground: `docs/REVIEW-23-07.md` (reviewed at `fd71c5e`, 2026-07-23; 11 parallel subsystem reviewers, each finding adversarially re-verified by an independent refuter), finding M12, verbatim: "Local send to a `Present` receiver silently drops the message on `HeapFull`. `scheduler/supervision_integration.rs:1004` — the code holds `&mut Process` under the slot lock and the parallel I/O path proves `ensure_space` is usable here, yet this path drops instead of collecting — silent, reachable message loss. (Related: closures with captured variables sent to an `Executing` receiver are dropped by the ETF encode path, making delivery race-dependent.)" Evidence pin for THIS brief: beamr main `a0359a2`.

RE-PIN AT `a0359a2` (the file DID drift — 149 lines changed between `fd71c5e` and `a0359a2` — but the cited construct did not move): `SchedulerLocalSendFacility::send_local` is at `supervision_integration.rs:915` (struct) / `:919-1074` (impl), UNMOVED from `fd71c5e`. The `Present` arm's non-telemetry drop is at `:1002-1018`, with the cited `.send(request.message, process.0.heap_mut())` at `:1008` — BYTE-IDENTICAL to `fd71c5e:1008`; the review's `:1004` is the `if process` head of that same block, also unmoved. Its telemetry twin is at `:977-1001` (`send_traced` at `:983`, drop at `:998-999`). BOTH ARMS DROP. The telemetry arm at least counts the loss (`record_message_dropped("mailbox_present")`); the non-telemetry arm — the DEFAULT build, and the one the gate battery compiles — drops with no observable trace whatsoever. The in-code comment is candid about it: "BEAM `!` cannot fail, so we still return Ok and drop the message ... a copy-into-mailbox failure (e.g. the receiver's young heap is full; beamr's bump allocator returns HeapFull rather than GCing) should never be silent." The comment names the true cause: BEAMR'S BUMP ALLOCATOR RETURNS `HeapFull` RATHER THAN GCING. That is a fixable precondition, not a law.

THE FIX IS ALREADY PROVEN USABLE AT THIS EXACT SEAM — three independent pieces of evidence, all at this head:
  (i) `gc::ensure_space(process: &mut Process, words: usize, live_x: usize)` (`crates/beamr/src/gc/mod.rs:149-170`) collects minor, falls back to major, then GROWS via `grow_to_next_capacity_with_max` in a loop until the request fits. In the `Present` arm the facility holds `process: &mut ScheduledProcess`, so `process.0` IS the `&mut Process` `ensure_space` wants — the borrow is already in hand, under the slot lock, with no re-entrancy.
  (ii) THE PARALLEL PATH THE REVIEW MEANS: `scheduler/timer_integration.rs:213-230` `copy_owned_message` does precisely this — `gc::ensure_space(process, message.total_words(), 256)`, map the `GcError`, then `copy_to_heap` + `push_owned`. And `scheduler/execution/core.rs:965-978` does it on the suspension-result path with the same `live_x = 256`. Collecting a `Present` receiver's heap from outside its slice is established practice in this crate, not a novel move.
  (iii) THE RETRY SHAPE IS ALREADY IN THIS VERY FILE: `supervision_integration.rs:2143-2155` (closure-spawn env copy) matches `Err(crate::mailbox::SendError::HeapFull(full))` and retries with a doubled heap, bounded by `CLOSURE_SPAWN_MAX_HEAP_WORDS` (`:2163`), returning a TYPED ERROR rather than dropping when the bound is hit. `mailbox::SendError::HeapFull(HeapFull)` (`mailbox/mod.rs:24-29`) carries `requested`/`available` (`process/heap.rs:23-40`), so the retry can be sized exactly instead of doubling blind.

THE SAME FAILURE HAS THREE DIFFERENT DISPOSITIONS IN THIS VM — found during re-pin, not in the review, and it is the strongest argument that this is a coherence defect and not a one-line patch. Identical `SendError::HeapFull` from the identical `mailbox::copy_term`:
  * `interpreter/opcodes/messaging.rs:97` (in-hand cross-process send) — `.map_err(send_error)?` -> `ExecError::HeapFull` -> propagates out of `run_loop`, UNCATCHABLE (the RF-004 class), sender dies.
  * `interpreter/opcodes/messaging.rs:182` (`send_to_self`) — same: uncatchable propagation, sender dies.
  * `supervision_integration.rs:1008` (facility, `Present`) — SILENT DROP, `Ok(())`.
None of the three collects. One VM, one failure, three answers, and the only path a user can observe is the one that kills the sender for a condition the GC could have cleared.

THE ETF SIBLING IS STILL LIVE AT `a0359a2` — VERIFIED AT THE BYTES, NOT INFERRED. `supervision_integration.rs:1039-1065`, the `Executing` arm: `crate::etf::encode::encode_term(request.message, &self.shared.atom_table)` -> on `Err(_error)`, `return Ok(())` — dropped. The rejection is real and unchanged: `crates/beamr/src/etf/encode.rs:574` and `:604` both `if closure.num_free() != 0 { ... }` refuse a captured-variable closure. The in-code `KNOWN LIMITATION` block (`:1049-1060`) states the consequence exactly: "a closure capturing variables sent to an *Executing* receiver is dropped here, even though the Present/in-hand path (`copy_term`) would deliver it faithfully." That is a RACE: the SAME send of the SAME closure to the SAME pid delivers or vanishes depending on whether the receiver happened to be mid-slice — and the non-telemetry build does not even count it (the `record_message_dropped("etf_encode")` at `:1062` is `#[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]`, and the gate battery builds default features only, per the review's own Low/hygiene note). Scope ruling below.

RESIDUAL DROP SITES, enumerated at `a0359a2` so the brief is honest about what it does and does not close: `:932-933` (absent/dead pid — CORRECT, BEAM semantics, not a defect), `:1068` (`ProcessSlot::Absent` — same), `:998-999` (telemetry `Present` drop), `:1016` (non-telemetry `Present` drop), `:1063` (`Executing` ETF drop).
task:
DESIGN STANCE (decided, with one carved fork OQ-A): the `Present` local-send path COLLECTS BEFORE IT DROPS, and when it genuinely cannot deliver it says so instead of returning `Ok(())` into the void. `!` stays infallible from the Erlang program's point of view — this brief does not add a failure mode to `send/2`; it removes a silent-success mode from the VM. Zero new wake paths, zero timers, zero configuration.

D1 COLLECT-THEN-RETRY (`Present`, both cfg arms). Replace the drop with: attempt the copy; on `Err(SendError::HeapFull(full))`, call `crate::gc::ensure_space(&mut process.0, full.requested(), 256)` and RETRY the copy exactly once; only a second failure reaches the terminal disposition (D3). `live_x = 256` matches the conservative full-register live set the sibling paths use (`timer_integration.rs:217`, `execution/core.rs:965`) — the receiver is parked in its slot, so all X registers are roots. `SendError::InvalidBoxedTerm` is NOT a heap condition and does not retry; it goes straight to D3. The two `#[cfg]` arms must be brought to IDENTICAL logic — a defect that exists in the default build and not in the telemetry build is how this one survived review-by-reading in the first place.

D2 THE ALIASING PROOF — the load-bearing correctness argument, and the reason this is not a one-liner. `ensure_space` runs a MOVING collector on the RECEIVER's heap. `request.message` is a `Term`. If that term points into the heap being collected, the retry copies from moved-or-freed memory — the exact H3/H4/H5 defect class from the same review, newly introduced. `native/local_send.rs:30-37` documents the invariant: "The `message` term references the *sender's* heap. The call is synchronous, performed inside the sender's slice while the sender body is alive." So for a genuine cross-process send the message is NOT in the receiver's heap and the collection cannot touch it. THE DRAFTER MUST PROVE THAT INVARIANT HOLDS ON EVERY PATH THAT REACHES THE `Present` ARM, not cite it: (a) live-mode cross-process — sender's slot is `Executing`, receiver is `Present`, distinct heaps, safe; (b) live-mode SELF-send — `messaging.rs:105-110` routes a bytecode self-send in-hand and never to the facility, and `local_send.rs`'s header note plus `supervision_integration.rs:924-930` state a NATIVE self-send lands in the sender's own `Executing` slot, never `Present`; VERIFY THIS AT THE BYTES rather than trusting the comment; (c) REPLAY mode — `:938-940` asserts "on a single replay thread no other pid can be Executing, so the receiver is always Present (or Absent)", which is precisely the regime where a self-send COULD find its own body `Present`. If any path can alias, the fix is to reserve BEFORE reading the message term or to re-derive it after, and the site says so in a comment. An unproven aliasing assumption here is a STOP.

D3 TERMINAL DISPOSITION — the honest end of the retry. After `ensure_space` + retry still fails (max heap reached: `grow_to_next_capacity_with_max` is bounded by `DEFAULT_MAX_HEAP_WORDS = 131_072`, `process/heap.rs:17,272`), or on `InvalidBoxedTerm`, the send MUST NOT return `Ok(())` silently. The recommended shape (the fork is OQ-A) is to widen `LocalSendError` (`native/local_send.rs:24-28`, currently the single variant `ReplayMismatch(String)`) with a delivery-failure variant carrying the pid and the `HeapFull` figures, and to have the caller in `messaging::send` map it the way `send_error` already maps the in-hand failure (`messaging.rs:356-361` -> `ExecError::from(HeapFull)`). That makes the facility path CONSISTENT WITH the in-hand path (`messaging.rs:97`) — the three-dispositions incoherence collapses to one — and turns an invisible loss into an observable, attributable VM error. The doc comments on `LocalSendError` and `LocalSendFacility` (`local_send.rs:19-23, 51-56`) that currently promise "`Err` only for a genuine replay-determinism mismatch" are amended in the same commit; leaving them stale is a STOP. Note for the tear: this makes an EXHAUSTED-HEAP send observable, which BEAM also does (a process that cannot grow its heap dies) — it does NOT make an ordinary send fallible.

D4 THE ETF SIBLING (`Executing`) — SCOPED IN, but as CLASSIFICATION + WALL, not as a codec build. Verified live at `a0359a2` (see purpose). Closing it properly requires symmetric closure ETF or a heap-fragment copy for the `Executing` case — a codec-design lane, materially larger than this one, and folding it in would let the `Present` fix wait on it. THIS LANE MUST: (i) make the drop OBSERVABLE IN EVERY BUILD, not only under `--features telemetry` — the non-telemetry drop at `:1063` is currently invisible in the default build the gate battery compiles; (ii) commit a RED-DOCUMENTED wall proving the race exists — same closure, same pid, delivered when `Present` and lost when `Executing` — as an `#[ignore]`d-with-reason or explicitly-asserting-current-behavior test that a future codec fix must flip, so the asymmetry can never be quietly forgotten again; (iii) record it in the R5 artifact with the codec work named as its closing lane. Anything beyond that is out of scope here and the handoff says so plainly. FORK: if the drafter finds at the bytes that the `Present` path's `copy_term` ALSO rejects free-variable closures (making the asymmetry nonexistent), (ii) becomes a proof of the SAME behavior on both arms and the row is downgraded — state the finding either way.

D5 RED FIRST (R1). A DETERMINISTIC HeapFull-at-send fixture. Determinism is achievable at the lib-test level with NO new API and NO knob: `Heap::with_max_heap_size(capacity, max_capacity)` is already `pub` (`process/heap.rs:278`), `Process::heap_mut()` returns `&mut Heap` (`process/mod.rs:385-387`), and this very file already hand-builds `ProcessSlot::Present(ScheduledProcess(child))` bodies for its tests (`:1380`, `:1490`, `:1636`, `:1981`). So: build a receiver whose heap is capped just below the message's word count, insert it Present, call `send_local`, assert. The assertion is DELIVERY-OR-ERROR, NEVER SILENT LOSS: either the mailbox depth increases by one and the term round-trips, or a typed error is returned — `Ok(())` with an unchanged mailbox is the RED. Twin legs: (a) cap ABOVE the message but with the free-space bump exhausted -> collect-and-deliver (the fix's whole point: this case must DELIVER, not error); (b) cap BELOW any possible fit -> typed error, never `Ok(())`. Both arms (`telemetry` and default) are exercised.

D6 SCOPE FENCE. M11 (per-sender FIFO inversion, `scheduler/execution/core.rs:442`) is an ORDERING defect on an adjacent path and is NOT reopened here — but the drafter must confirm the retry does not perturb the enqueue ORDER on the success path (the copy is retried, the enqueue still happens exactly once, in the same position). The `Absent`/dead-pid drops (`:932-933`, `:1068`) are CORRECT BEAM semantics and stay. C1/C2 and the H3/H4/H5 GC-move class are other lanes; D2's aliasing proof must not introduce an instance of the latter.

OQ-A (carved for the tear): D3's `LocalSendError` widening vs. the narrower alternative of keeping the facility signature and having it kill the receiver with a heap-exhaustion exit (BEAM's own answer to a process that cannot grow). Recommendation: D3 as written — it is symmetric with the in-hand path that already exists at `messaging.rs:97`, it attributes the failure to the send site, and it does not invent a new process-death path. The alternative is arguably more BEAM-faithful and the tear should rule.

requirements.title: RED — deterministic HeapFull-at-send fixture asserting delivery-or-error, never silent loss
requirements.spec: Per D5: a test that caps a `Present` receiver's heap via the existing `Heap::with_max_heap_size` + `Process::heap_mut()` (no new API, no config knob), inserts it as `ProcessSlot::Present` using this file's established hand-built-slot pattern (`:1380`/`:1490`/`:1636`/`:1981`), and drives `SchedulerLocalSendFacility::send_local` with a message that cannot fit the current free space. Two legs: (a) collectable/growable -> MUST DELIVER; (b) genuinely unfittable -> MUST return a typed error. `Ok(())` with an unchanged mailbox is the RED condition in BOTH legs.
acceptance: The test FAILS at `a0359a2` in both legs — leg (a) because the current code drops a message the GC could have made room for, leg (b) because the current code returns `Ok(())` on unrecoverable loss. The RED transcript is recorded in the commit body
DETERMINISTIC: ten consecutive isolated runs produce the identical outcome. No timing dependence, no sleep, no retry loop in the test — the heap cap forces the condition exactly (NO-POLLING)
Run under BOTH cfg arms — default features AND `--features telemetry` — because the two arms are separate code (`:977-1001` vs `:1002-1018`) and the default build is the one the gate battery compiles
The assertion is on OBSERVED DELIVERY (mailbox depth +1 and the term's value round-tripped), not on the return value alone — a fix that returns `Ok(())` without enqueueing must stay red

requirements.title: `Present` arm collects before it drops — both cfg arms, identical logic
requirements.spec: Per D1: on `Err(SendError::HeapFull(full))` call `crate::gc::ensure_space(&mut process.0, full.requested(), 256)` and retry the copy exactly once, mirroring `timer_integration.rs:213-230` and `execution/core.rs:965-978`. `SendError::InvalidBoxedTerm` does not retry. The `#[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]` (`:977-1001`) and `#[cfg(not(...))]` (`:1002-1018`) branches carry IDENTICAL delivery logic, differing only in the telemetry call.
acceptance: R1 leg (a) goes GREEN: a message that did not fit the free space is DELIVERED after collection, with its value intact

Exactly one retry — no unbounded loop, no doubling ladder, no polling. `ensure_space` already collects, majors, and grows internally (`gc/mod.rs:149-170`); a second failure means the heap max is genuinely reached
Both cfg arms are byte-comparable in delivery logic (a reviewer can diff them and see only the telemetry line); a test exercises both

The stale in-code comments at `:991-998` and `:1011-1015` — which currently ARGUE FOR the drop — are rewritten to state the new contract. Leaving a comment that documents the removed behavior is a STOP
The success-path enqueue happens exactly once and in the same position as before — the retry re-copies, it does not re-enqueue (D6: M11's ordering surface is not perturbed)

requirements.title: The aliasing proof — `ensure_space` on the receiver cannot invalidate the message term
requirements.spec: Per D2: enumerate every path that reaches the `Present` arm (live cross-process, live native self-send, live bytecode self-send, replay-mode delivery) and prove at the bytes — not by citing the doc comment — that `request.message` never points into the heap `ensure_space` collects. Where the invariant holds, record the mechanism in a comment AT THE SITE. Where any path can alias, reserve before reading the term or re-derive it after, and say so at the site.
acceptance: A written enumeration of the reaching paths with, for each, the code site that establishes the sender's body is NOT the receiver's body (or the handling if it can be). `native/local_send.rs:30-37`'s invariant is CORROBORATED at the bytes, not merely quoted

The REPLAY regime is specifically addressed: `:938-940` claims the receiver is always `Present` under replay, which is the one regime where a self-send could find its own body Present. Either it is proven unreachable or it is handled
ZERO new instances of the H3/H4/H5 stale-Term-across-a-moving-collection class — the same review's rank-2 finding. A reviewer can point at the reserve point and the read point and see the ordering
The proof lands as a comment at the call site, not only in the commit body — the next reader of this function must find it there

requirements.title: Terminal disposition — unrecoverable loss is reported, not returned as `Ok(())`
requirements.spec: Per D3 (subject to the OQ-A ruling): widen `LocalSendError` (`native/local_send.rs:24-28`) with a delivery-failure variant carrying the target pid and the `HeapFull` requested/available figures; map it at the caller consistently with the in-hand path's `send_error` (`messaging.rs:356-361`). Amend the now-false doc comments on `LocalSendError` (`:19-23`) and `LocalSendFacility::send_local` (`:51-56`) in the SAME commit.
acceptance: R1 leg (b) goes GREEN: an unfittable message yields a typed error naming the pid and the heap figures; `Ok(())` on unrecoverable loss no longer exists on this path (grep: no `return Ok(())` remains in the `Present` arm's failure handling)

The three-dispositions incoherence is CLOSED or explicitly narrowed: the facility path and the in-hand path (`messaging.rs:97`) now answer the same failure the same way, and the handoff states exactly which of the three sites still differ and why
The `Absent`/dead-pid `Ok(())` returns (`:932-933`, `:1068`) are UNCHANGED — a dead target is a correct silent drop under BEAM semantics and is not swept up by this change
Every `LocalSendError` match site compiles (the enum widening is compile-forced); ZERO `_ =>` arms are introduced to dodge the exhaustive match
The doc comments that promised "`Err` only for a genuine replay-determinism mismatch" are corrected; no comment in the tree still documents the removed behavior

requirements.title: The `Executing` ETF sibling — verified live, made observable in every build, and walled as a known race
requirements.spec: Per D4: the captured-variable-closure drop at `supervision_integration.rs:1039-1065` (rejection source `etf/encode.rs:574,604`, `num_free() != 0`) is CONFIRMED LIVE at `a0359a2`. This lane does not build symmetric closure ETF. It makes the drop observable without the `telemetry` feature, commits a wall that pins the race so it cannot be forgotten, and records the codec lane that closes it.
acceptance: The `Executing`-arm encode failure is observable in the DEFAULT build — the current `record_message_dropped("etf_encode")` at `:1062` is `#[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]` only, and the gate battery compiles default features (the review's own Low/hygiene note). The chosen mechanism adds NO config knob and NO polling

A committed test pins the asymmetry at current bytes: the same captured-variable closure sent to the same pid is delivered when the receiver is `Present` and lost when `Executing`. It asserts today's behavior explicitly (or is `#[ignore]`d with the reason inline) so that the future codec fix MUST come back and flip it

PER D4's FORK, stated either way: if `copy_term` on the `Present` path also rejects free-variable closures, the asymmetry does not exist — the finding is recorded and the wall becomes a same-behavior proof instead
The R6 artifact row names the codec lane (symmetric closure ETF, or a heap-fragment copy for the `Executing` case) as the closing work; the handoff says plainly that this brief does NOT close it

requirements.title: Drop-site census — every `Ok(())`-on-undelivered in the local-send path classified
requirements.spec: A committed table enumerating every point in `SchedulerLocalSendFacility::send_local` (and the in-hand siblings at `messaging.rs:97`, `:182`) where a message can fail to arrive, each classified as CORRECT-BY-BEAM-SEMANTICS (dead/absent target), FIXED-IN-THIS-LANE, or KNOWN-AND-WALLED with its closing lane named.
acceptance: The census covers, at minimum, the five sites pinned at `a0359a2`: `:932-933` (absent entry), `:998-999` (telemetry Present), `:1016` (non-telemetry Present), `:1063` (Executing ETF), `:1068` (`ProcessSlot::Absent`) — plus the in-hand dispositions at `messaging.rs:97` and `:182`
Every row states its classification AND its reason; zero rows read `probably fine` or elide siblings
The three-dispositions finding (propagate-uncaught / silent-drop / silent-drop for one failure) is written down explicitly as the coherence defect it is, with the post-fix state of each
The artifact is committed to the tree, not only described in the commit body

boundaries: `!` STAYS INFALLIBLE TO ERLANG. This brief removes a silent-success mode from the VM; it does not add a failure mode to `send/2` for any message that can be delivered. A change that makes ordinary sends fallible is a STOP.
DEAD/ABSENT TARGET REMAINS A SILENT DROP (`:932-933`, `:1068`) — correct BEAM semantics, untouched.
NO STALE TERM ACROSS A MOVING COLLECTION. R3's aliasing proof is a hard gate, not documentation: introducing an H3/H4/H5-class instance while fixing M12 is a STOP.
ORDERING UNPERTURBED: M11 (per-sender FIFO inversion, `scheduler/execution/core.rs:442`) is NOT reopened, and the retry must not change enqueue position or count on the success path.

BOTH `#[cfg]` ARMS MOVE TOGETHER. A delivery behavior that differs between the default and `telemetry` builds is exactly how this defect survived; the arms end this lane with identical delivery logic and both are tested.

ZERO new `#[allow]` of any kind; no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside `cfg(test)`; no `_ =>` catch-all arms introduced to dodge an exhaustive match — the `LocalSendError` widening in R4 is compile-forced and must be handled honestly at every site.
NO-POLLING: no new wake paths, no timers, no sleep/retry loops in production code. Exactly one retry after exactly one `ensure_space`; the wake path (`wake_process`, `:1072`) is unchanged.
NO NEW CONFIG KNOBS — no configurable retry count, no heap-cap setting, no 'strict delivery' mode. The R1 heap cap is achieved with existing `pub` API inside `cfg(test)` only.

BOTH wasm32 CLOSURES STAY GREEN. `native/local_send.rs` and `interpreter/opcodes/messaging.rs` are shared code compiled for the threaded AND the cooperative closure; `cargo check -p beamr-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --locked` and the wasm-tests leg must be green at the final head. If an `ExecError` variant is added, `crates/beamr-wasm/src/reasons.rs` moves in the SAME commit with an additive row and the WPORT-5 coverage wall extends.

THE ETF CODEC IS NOT REBUILT HERE. R5 observes, walls, and records the closure-ETF asymmetry; symmetric closure encoding (or a heap-fragment copy for the `Executing` case) is a separate lane and the handoff names it.
verification: Build-leg bar: the full release battery at the FINAL head — `cargo fmt --all --check`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` with Compiling lines visible (fresh, not cached); `cargo check -p beamr-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --locked`; the wasm-tests leg; `cargo test --workspace`; PLUS a `--features telemetry` test leg for the touched module, because the two `#[cfg]` arms are separate code and the default battery only compiles one of them. Prohibition greps: zero new `#[allow]`; no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside `cfg(test)` in touched files; no `return Ok(())` remaining in the `Present` arm's failure handling; no `_ =>` added to any `LocalSendError` match. 10x isolation runs on both new walls, both cfg arms. FAIL-FIRST, recorded and reverted: revert R2 -> R1 leg (a) goes red (the collectable message is dropped); revert R4 -> R1 leg (b) goes red (`Ok(())` on unrecoverable loss); restore. PIN-SHIFT RE-VERIFY at the ACTUAL build base (this brief is pinned at `a0359a2` and the file DRIFTED 149 lines between the review commit and this pin — re-read before writing a line): `SchedulerLocalSendFacility` (`supervision_integration.rs:915-1074`), specifically the `Present` telemetry arm (`:977-1001`), the `Present` default arm (`:1002-1018`), the `Executing` ETF arm (`:1039-1066`), the `Absent` arms (`:932-933`, `:1068`), and the in-file HeapFull retry precedent (`:2143-2163`); `native/local_send.rs` in full (61 lines); `interpreter/opcodes/messaging.rs:85-110`, `:170-185`, `send_error` `:356-361`; `gc::ensure_space` (`gc/mod.rs:149-170`); the sibling ensure_space precedents (`timer_integration.rs:213-230`, `execution/core.rs:965-978`); `mailbox::SendError` (`mailbox/mod.rs:24-44`) and `HeapFull` (`process/heap.rs:23-40`, `DEFAULT_MAX_HEAP_WORDS` at `:17`); `etf/encode.rs:574`, `:604`. Handoff carries: the aliasing enumeration in full, the OQ-A ruling with reasons, the ETF-sibling finding (live/not-live and which of D4's fork applied), the drop-site census, and the post-fix state of all three dispositions of `SendError::HeapFull`.
